final_answer:
Every natural transformation \(\Theta:W_S\Rightarrow W_T\) has the form

\[
\Theta_X(s,f)=\bigl(\alpha(s),\ t\mapsto f(\beta(s,t))\bigr),
\]

for some functions

\[
\alpha:S\to T,\qquad \beta:S\times T\to S.
\]

Indeed, the first component is forced by evaluating at \(X=1\), and the second component is a natural map \(X^S\to X\), hence evaluation at some element of \(S\).

The counit condition gives

\[
f(\beta(s,\alpha(s)))=f(s)
\]

for all \(f\), so

\[
\beta(s,\alpha(s))=s.
\]

Now compute the comultiplication condition. Writing \(b_s(t)=\beta(s,t)\), it forces

\[
\alpha(b_s(t))=t
\]

and

\[
b_{b_s(t)}=b_s
\]

for all \(s\in S,\ t\in T\). Thus each \(b_s:T\to S\) is a section of \(\alpha\), contains \(s\), and is constant on its own image.

Therefore the data are exactly:

1. a map \(\alpha:S\to T\) whose fibers all have size \(q\);
2. a partition of \(S\) into \(q\) blocks, each block containing exactly one element from each fiber of \(\alpha\).

The number of possible \(\alpha\)'s is

\[
\frac{(qn)!}{(q!)^n}.
\]

For a fixed \(\alpha\), the number of such transversal partitions is

\[
\frac{(q!)^n}{q!}=(q!)^{n-1},
\]

since each fiber can be bijected with \(q\) block labels, modulo global relabeling of the blocks.

Hence the total number is

\[
\frac{(qn)!}{(q!)^n}\cdot (q!)^{n-1}
=
\frac{(qn)!}{q!}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{(qn)!}{q!}}
\]
